title: Strip Out The AI-Driven ASP Inflation & 2026’s $1 Trillion Becomes $625 Billion
gist: Future Horizons' October 2026 bulletin says semiconductor growth is driven by AI infrastructure and ASP inflation; stripping out AI-related price inflation would cut 2026's $1 trillion market to about $625 billion. WSTS data show August sales up 156.3% year on year, and Malcolm Penn warns against assuming this continues.

themes.theme: AI-driven ASP inflation in 2026 chip market

insights.claim: Future Horizons argues that removing AI-related price inflation would shrink the apparent 2026 semiconductor market from $1 trillion to about $625 billion, implying roughly 37% of headline value comes from AI-driven pricing.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Headline market size overstates underlying unit demand, so cycle-peak risk is higher than top-line growth suggests.
insights.quote: Strip Out The AI-Driven ASP Inflation & 2026’s $1 Trillion Becomes $625 Billion

insights.claim: The expansion is concentrated in specialised AI infrastructure rather than being supported by broad unit demand growth as in previous cycles.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Narrow breadth makes the sector more exposed to a pullback in hyperscaler capex.

insights.claim: Expensive AI chips face affordability constraints in the conventional applications that historically sustained the industry.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Limits spillover of AI pricing into broader semiconductor demand.
insights.locator: Expensive AI chips also face affordability constraints

insights.claim: The bulletin's concern is the present imbalance between infrastructure spending and commercially meaningful end products, plus dependence on inflated prices, while accepting AI's long-term potential.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Monitor monetization of AI end products as the validation test for current capex.
insights.locator: The bulletin accepts AI’s substantial long term potential

insights.claim: Malcolm Penn advises companies to benefit from current growth but not assume ASP increases continue indefinitely, and to keep contingency plans in case conditions weaken.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A cautionary signal from a long-standing industry forecaster late in a record up-cycle.

insights.claim: Per cited WSTS figures, August 2026 semiconductor sales rose 156.3% versus August 2025, and sales adjusted for the five-week month rose 23.3% month on month versus 13.6% the prior month.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Acceleration in monthly growth shows the boom was still strengthening as of August.
insights.locator: According to the bulletin’s cited WSTS figures

insights.claim: Integrated circuits grew 175.9% year on year in August while discretes grew only 8.4% and optoelectronics 9.2%, showing the surge is almost entirely in ICs.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Divergence suggests the boom is not broad across the semiconductor product spectrum.
insights.locator: Integrated circuits accounted for most of the expansion

insights.claim: Current growth is described as unprecedented, exceeding earlier peaks of 59.3% in June 2000 and 66.6% in January 2010.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Growth far above prior cyclical peaks is a historical marker of an extreme point in the cycle.
insights.locator: The report describes current growth as unprecedented

insights.claim: The boom is attributed to confidence that AI will transform society and the global economy, encouraging hyperscalers to commit enormous sums to infrastructure.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Demand rests on belief-driven capex, which can reverse if confidence changes.
insights.locator: It attributes the boom to confidence
